about: The jsdom-parity gap ledger (Phase 0 of the parity plan). Generated from scripts/surface-diff.mjs and scripts/area-diff.mjs against the oracle below; groups are classified by hand because the raw member counts repeat the same systematic gaps on every interface. scripts/check-gaps.mjs re-runs the surface inventory and fails if the recorded surface facts drift. Semantic area scores are snapshots with their run parameters; they change only when the generators or the engine change, and Phase 2 drives them to full agreement (or to an adjudicated note, where jsdom itself departs from the spec).
outOfScope: Layout values (getBoundingClientRect and friends return 0) — README non-goal
Canvas, iframe contents, real WebSocket/EventSource/Worker transports, media decoding — README non-goals
jsdom's 29 underscore-prefixed window internals — not public API (design doc section 1)

findings.what: RESOLVED in Phase 2 (2026-11-04): the on* handler is now a slot in the listener list, claimed the first time the handler is set (IDL) or a dispatch reaches an element carrying the attribute, and kept across null and re-set — jsdom's model, which the old trailing-call model disagreed with whenever listeners registered after the first set. A handler assigned as a plain property on an accessor-less EventTarget (the shims' WebSocket and friends) still fires after the list.

DECIDED in Phase 2 and confirmed by the author on 2026-11-04: follow the DOM spec and real browsers, not jsdom. At the target jsdom runs capture listeners before bubble ones (each group in registration order); the spec's inner invoke runs the target's list in registration order, current browsers agree with the spec, and this package's own event test pins registration order (c before C). Every remaining events divergence in the 20-program run (14/20; 34/40 at 40 programs) reduces to this one ordering and its interaction with stopImmediatePropagation. The divergence is therefore accepted deliberately; jsdom's at-target ordering will not be copied.

RESOLVED in Phase 4 (2026-11-04), found by @testing-library/dom's suite: dispatch flattened shadow trees — the path stepped from a shadow root to its host for every event, so non-composed events leaked out and composed ones were not retargeted. The path now stops at the shadow root unless the event is composed, listeners outside a tree see the host as the target (and a retargeted host hears even a non-bubbling event, as the target of its own tree), isConnected steps through the host (an element in a shadow tree of a connected host is connected, and focusable), and the engine's own focus events are composed. One author expectation changed (nativedom-api's attachShadow test pinned a non-composed event crossing; it now pins the boundary both ways).

RESOLVED in Phase 2 (2026-11-04): compareBoundaryPoints now throws WrongDocumentError when the two ranges' roots differ, as the spec's algorithm states (and as comparePoint already did). The Phase 0 note's 'closer to browsers' reading was wrong; the spec text governs.

RESOLVED in Phase 2 (2026-11-04): cloneContents (and with it extractContents) now follows the spec's clone: a node the range cuts into is cloned shallowly and filled with the part inside, where the old code took only the wholly-contained nodes and the two cut texts and dropped every partial wrapper (

around a cut paragraph, and so on). The area went 2/20 -> 20/20 (37/40 at 40 programs, the rest sharing the fixed programs).

RESOLVED in Phase 2 (2026-11-04): value, checkedness and selectedness are now state of their own, seeded by their defaults (the value/checked/selected attributes, a textarea's text) and parting from them once set — the spec's dirty-flag model, which jsdom implements. This one change carries the four findings the area opened with: selectedIndex = -1 deselects (and reads back -1), input[type=number] values are sanitised, checking a radio unchecks its group, and form.reset() — now firing its event first and honouring cancelation — restores defaults by clearing the state. One author test pinned the old conflation (setting .value wrote the attribute, a textarea's .value rewrote its text); its two affected expectations were updated to the separated model and the change is flagged in the commit and the Phase 2 report. Not covered: type=range value clamping and the date/time family sanitisation.

RESOLVED in Phase 4 (2026-11-04), found by @testing-library/dom's suite: `checked`/`defaultChecked` were accessors on HTMLElement (and a generic `selected` reflection sat beside the option's own), so 'checked' in element was true for every element and libraries branching on it never reached their aria-checked fallback. They now live only on HTMLInputElement / HTMLOptionElement, as in the spec and jsdom. In the same round: a hidden input's `labels` now answers null (not an empty list), which is what the label helpers branch on.

The systematic divergences are jsdom's computed style being poorer: it returns '' for width/opacity/font-size initial values and leaves var() unresolved, where ours resolves (width: auto/7px, opacity: 1, font-size: 16px). This area's oracle is the spec and browsers, not jsdom; do not 'fix' toward jsdom. Real gaps, if any, surface only against a browser reference. Phase 2 review (2026-11-04): re-confirmed — the systematic divergences remain jsdom-side poverty, not gaps here; no style work was needed or done.

jsdom 30 serializes a zero computed length as "0" where browsers (and jsdom 26) answer "0px"; ours answers "0px". The package's computed-style comparison test carries a carve-out for exactly this pair. Do not 'fix' toward jsdom.

RESOLVED in Phase 2 (2026-11-04): the C tree builder (csrc/nativedom.h nd_build) now does the standard's work the htmlparser2 port omitted — implied table sections/rows in fragments as well as documents, foster parenting of content that cannot live in a table, the adoption agency in simplified form (an active-formatting-elements list with reconstruction; parser closes now carry the tag whose processing closed the element, and stray formatting end tags arrive as their own event), the standard's adjusted SVG tag names (foreignObject), and isindex/command as ordinary elements (they left the void list). DOMParser's XML types no longer go through the HTML parser: a small strict XML parser in the guest builds them (malformed input yields the parsererror document), and tagName/nodeName upper-case only for HTML elements in HTML documents. Remainders: the full adoption agency's furthest-block shuffle is not attempted; CDATA sections become text (no CDATA node kind) and serialise escaped; XML namespaces are not resolved (names keep their qualified spelling); processing instructions in XML input are skipped; createElementNS keeps the given case only through the parser's adjustment, not for hand-made names.

Element name case follows from the tree-construction fix: localName is the adjusted name for foreign elements, namespaceURI treats integration points (foreignObject, annotation-xml with encoding text/html, svg desc/title) as HTML for their children only. MathML text integration points (mi/mo/mn/ms/mtext children) are not given the HTML namespace — recorded as a known miss, no corpus case covers it.

RESOLVED in Phase 4 (2026-11-04), found by @testing-library/dom's suite: in a fragment build (innerHTML, parseFragment) an <html> or <body> start tag made a nested element; the standard ignores the token and the content flows into the context. The builder now skips both tags and their closes in fragment builds only (a document build is unchanged).

semantic.run: scripts/area-diff.mjs, 20 programs x 60 steps per area

groups.what: The aria* IDL reflection properties (ariaAtomic, ariaBusy, ariaChecked, ...) are absent from Element instances; the attributes themselves work. RESOLVED in Phase 1 (2026-11-03): all 41 string reflections are defined on Element with their exact attribute names (not a mechanical kebab-casing: ariaValueNow mirrors aria-valuenow, ariaReadOnly mirrors aria-readonly, and so on).

Six legacy Node constants (ATTRIBUTE_NODE, CDATA_SECTION_NODE, ENTITY_NODE, ENTITY_REFERENCE_NODE, NOTATION_NODE, PROCESSING_INSTRUCTION_NODE) are absent from instance prototype chains; the common constants (ELEMENT_NODE, TEXT_NODE, the DOCUMENT_POSITION_* set) are present. RESOLVED in Phase 1 (2026-11-03): the six constants are defined on Node and its prototype.

The window on* handler properties (onclick, onload, ...) are not globals. Element-level on* IDL handlers do work (see the events area). RESOLVED in Phase 1 (2026-11-03): the shared handler definitions now also apply to the global object, with the window's own extra events (afterprint, beforeunload, message, popstate, storage, unload, the webkit-prefixed animation/transition ends, ...) added; 118 on* properties answer on the window and setting one registers it in the same dispatch path (invoke reads node['on'+type] for every step, the window included).

Plain window properties are absent: the scroll offsets, the screen position, name, status, origin, frameElement, length, event, external, and the BarProp-valued bar properties (locationbar, menubar, personalbar, scrollbars, statusbar, toolbar — the BarProp class itself is in the unexposed group). Atomics and WebAssembly also appear in the oracle's window only because it runs on Node; they are not counted here. The Location exposure (Phase 1) also gives locationbar & friends a natural future home: they are BarProp instances pointing at the same window. RESOLVED in Phase 1 (2026-11-03): the scalar properties are defined in boot.js (offsets 0, name/status empty, origin from the location, frameElement null, length 0, event undefined) and the bars are BarProp instances.

The class is not exposed as a window global, while objects of it are reachable and work (classList, dataset, MutationObserver records, location/history/navigator were all measured live). instanceof checks and name lookups fail. RESOLVED in Phase 1 (2026-11-03): all seventeen are exposed with their prototypes — DOMTokenList, MutationRecord, History, Navigator, Screen, Performance, DOMStringMap, Location, StyleSheet, MediaList, StyleSheetList, FileList, RadioNodeList, DOMImplementation, HTMLDocument, BarProp, External.

Genuinely absent interfaces and window functions. jsdom 30 added most of the CSSRule family (typed rule classes, CSSRuleList, CSSStyleProperties), the device-motion/orientation events, BeforeUnloadEvent, BlobEvent, PromiseRejectionEvent and QuotaExceededError to the missing set. Phase 1 progress: queueMicrotask was already present (a stale classification); the window functions arrived in boot.js — dialogs and window management as the no-answers jsdom's shape suggests (confirm false, prompt null, open null), postMessage delivering a real MessageEvent to the window itself, webkitURL as the URL alias, and Crypto as the crypto object's interface. Then the constructor batch: Option and Audio as document shortcut constructors next to Image (whose prototype is now the image element's, so instanceof works there too); XMLDocument as a prototype layer createDocument and XML DOMParser results take; CDATASection and ProcessingInstruction as interfaces (no HTML document can hold their nodes); the customElements registry object on a CustomElementRegistry prototype; AbstractRange as the layer above Range.prototype and StaticRange as a real constructor over its init dictionary. Then the event batch: BeforeUnloadEvent, BlobEvent, CloseEvent, PromiseRejectionEvent, DeviceOrientationEvent and DeviceMotionEvent through the subclass helper (the motion component interfaces as null-valued prototypes); QuotaExceededError as a DOMException subclass in shims.js; and the XHR family's two interfaces — XMLHttpRequest now extends XMLHttpRequestEventTarget, chained to the real EventTarget in boot.js, and each request's upload is an XMLHttpRequestUpload. Then the element interfaces: the table family (caption, col/colgroup, thead/tbody/tfoot), dir, frame, frameset and marquee joined the tag-class table, SVGSwitchElement the SVG one, and SVGTitleElement is recognised by namespace and name (<title> stays an HTML tag in the mapping). NodeIterator and TreeWalker existed as factories; their products now carry the interfaces' prototypes (and the iterator's flag is spelled pointerBeforeReferenceNode, as in the spec — it was pointerBeforeReference). The members the newly visible interfaces revealed were filled in the same pass: table sections gained rows/insertRow/deleteRow, the legacy elements their reflections, elements generally gained the on* extras, getAttributeNodeNS/setAttributeNodeNS, webkitMatchesSelector and translate, and a frameset carries the window handler set. Two shape notes: iterator/walker members live on the instances, not the (empty) prototypes, and frame contentDocument/contentWindow answer null (frame content is a non-goal). The navigator's plugins and mimeTypes are empty PluginArray/MimeTypeArray instances (no plugins are registered), with Plugin and MimeType as their (unconstructable) interfaces. Then the CSS rule family: CSSRule with the spec's type constants (on the constructor and the prototype), the rule classes in their spec hierarchy (Grouping/Condition over media, supports, container, layer-block and scope; import, font-face, page, keyframes/keyframe, namespace, counter-style, layer-statement, nested declarations), a CSSRuleList that is the rules array wearing the interface's prototype, and parseSheetFlat classifying @-rules for real — nested rules parsed recursively with parentRule links, sheets stamping parentStyleSheet, @import answering href/media/an empty styleSheet, keyframe selectors normalised (from is 0%). A rule's style is now a CSSStyleProperties (a CSSStyleDeclaration subclass) with a working store — setProperty and removeProperty included — where it was a plain snapshot object. Types without a spec constant answer 0 (container, layer, scope). The last batch: the SVG value interfaces (the animated className/href/viewBox pairs wear SVGAnimatedString and SVGAnimatedRect/SVGRect; the rest are interfaces awaiting values), installed as globals by boot.js rather than registered — an animated value is all named properties, and the bridge's class wrappers would keep host-side baseVal writes local. XPathExpression prototypes createExpression's product, and XPathException is an Error subclass with the legacy codes. ElementInternals arrived with attachInternals: the real shadow root, an inert form side (these elements are not form-associated here), a standing all-valid validity, and the spec's gates (custom elements only, once). What remains is Window alone: the interface of the global object itself, whose prototype cannot be swapped without disturbing the runtime and the bridge — recorded as the one deliberate remainder of the surface.

jsdom 30 (cssstyle v6) no longer enumerates its CSS property-name database on CSSStyleDeclaration: the 1563-name gap recorded against jsdom 26 collapsed to 19 chain-visible names, which are Object.prototype helpers and the CSSStyleDeclaration methods themselves (cssText, getPropertyValue, setProperty, ...) — ours implements the methods but does not surface them to the chain walk the same way. Computed-style behaviour is covered by the style area, not here. The remaining 19 names were the CSSStyleDeclaration interface's own members (cssText, getPropertyValue, setProperty, item, length, parentRule and the Object.prototype helpers seen through the chain): the registered constructor was an empty function in computed.js while the real prototype lived on nativedom's StyleDecl. RESOLVED in Phase 1 (2026-11-03): one constructor — nativedom's, renamed CSSStyleDeclaration — serves el.style and getComputedStyle, installed as a global by boot.js and kept off the bridge's window table like DOMStringMap. The 10 that remain are the Object.prototype helpers (__defineGetter__, hasOwnProperty, valueOf, ...): they answer at runtime through the prototype chain (verified on a live style object) but the walker does not enumerate them on ours, whose style objects are Proxies — the same class of enumeration artefact as the collections-shape group.

Text: splitText and wholeText are absent; CharacterData lacks nextElementSibling/previousElementSibling; Text lacks assignedSlot. RESOLVED in Phase 1 (2026-11-03): splitText and wholeText are implemented on Text, assignedSlot answers null, and CharacterData has the element-sibling getters.

A Document instance is missing 34 names: legacy members (anchors, applets, captureEvents, clear, close, open, plugins, releaseEvents, write, writeln, embeds), factory methods for absent node types (createAttributeNS, createCDATASection, createProcessingInstruction), getElementsByTagNameNS, the implementation property, 12 on* handler properties, and the 6 legacy Node constants counted in their own group. NEARLY RESOLVED in Phase 1 (2026-11-03): of the 49 names the member walk found missing, 48 are now answered from Document.prototype (URL/documentURI via defaultView, contentType text/html on HTMLDocument.prototype, compatMode, the UTF-8 aliases, lastModified, referrer, readyState complete, hidden/visibilityState as jsdom's true/prerender, currentScript null, hasFocus false, dir reflected to the root element, a prototype cookie jar for non-page documents, the eight legacy collections, getElementsByName, captureEvents/releaseEvents no-ops, open/write/writeln/close/clear, createAttributeNS, createCDATASection throwing NotSupportedError as jsdom does for HTML documents, createEvent over the window's event classes, and the Document's own on* handlers). The one remaining name is createProcessingInstruction: jsdom creates a node of type 7, and this engine has no processing-instruction node factory (its parser reads one as a comment), so it waits on C work. Phase 3 (2026-11-04): the page's own document now takes these from the visual state the facade plumbs down (pretendToBeVisual): visible/not-hidden when visual, prerender/hidden when not; secondary documents keep true/prerender, and hasFocus answers per document — false until an element of it is focused, true from then on (jsdom's behaviour, blur included).

VERIFIED on live objects (Phase 1, first task): an enumeration artefact. attributes/childNodes/options/form.elements all carry working item()/namedItem()/getNamedItem(), index access and correct lengths in ours; the surface walker misses them because the guest does not enumerate those methods on the prototype chain. The sole real miss found is NamedNodeMap.getNamedItemNS (jsdom has it, ours does not). Ours is a superset in one place: namedItem also exists on our attributes/NodeList where jsdom has none. getNamedItemNS was added in Phase 1 (2026-11-03) alongside the Text members; Document and Element also gained getElementsByTagNameNS (namespace accepted, plain search — recorded under document-legacy).

facade.checked: 2026-11-04, jsdom 30.1.3, against the documented basic usage

findings.what: RESOLVED (2026-11-04, at the user's direction): the cookieJar option is implemented. The package ships a CookieJar with tough-cookie's synchronous surface (setCookieSync / getCookieStringSync / getCookiesSync, RFC 6265 domain and path scoping, Secure, HttpOnly, max-age/expires; no public-suffix list, no persistence), accepts any jar with that surface — a real tough-cookie jar included, verified in both directions against jsdom — and defaults to a fresh jar per JSDOM, readable as dom.cookieJar. The page's document.cookie delegates to the jar per access (HttpOnly filtered out; a script's own HttpOnly attribute ignored, as the RFC requires), the page's requests carry its cookies, and responses' Set-Cookie headers land in it (the engine's fetch path, and fromURL itself). At engine level (createDOM/openPage) the same option wires the same hooks; without it a page keeps the small per-page jar it always had.

RESOLVED in Phase 3 (2026-11-04): the option was accepted and ignored. It is now plumbed (facade -> engine `visual` -> boot): without it there is no requestAnimationFrame/cancelAnimationFrame, visibilityState is "prerender", hidden is true; with it the document is visible. document.hasFocus() follows jsdom's model in both modes — false until an element is focused, true from then on. The engine's own default stays visual (it renders pages); secondary documents stay prerender/unfocused.

RESOLVED in Phase 3 (2026-11-04) for the channels that exist: page script errors and unhandled rejections reach the virtual console as jsdomError with type "unhandled-exception", as jsdom classifies them. Remainders: jsdom also emits type "resource-loading" for a failed subresource element load and "not-implemented" notices for window.scrollTo/alert and the like; ours does not classify a failed request's initiator (a page fetch and a script load look alike in the log) and its stubs are silent, so neither is emitted.

RESOLVED in Phase 3 (2026-11-04): fetched (and byte-passed) pages are decoded by the content type's charset, then a byte-order mark, then a <meta charset> in the first bytes, then UTF-8 — jsdom's order. Redirects were already followed and the final URL used.

CHECKED in Phase 3 (2026-11-04) with scripts/env-diff.mjs (both windows through the package's installWindow): nothing a test can use is missing — the only names jsdom's environment has that ours does not are Window (the recorded surface remainder), Atomics/WebAssembly (the host runtime showing through jsdom's window) and jsdom's _-prefixed internals (out of scope). Ours installs a superset (the SVG interfaces, observers and stream classes jsdom lacks).

RESOLVED (2026-11-04): C fast-path for property sets and invocations, schema caching, tagName/infoOf optimization, and microtask integration reduced 3,000-node build from 149 ms (~3.5x jsdom) to 59.6 ms (~1.4x jsdom), achieving 1.30x ratio on build+read (well below the 2.0x guard line), with host-driven 1,000-node appendChild outperforming JSDOM (37.8 ms vs 46.0 ms). Memory stays flat across cycles.

RESOLVED in Phase 4 (2026-11-04), found by @testing-library/dom's suite, three bridge defects around host functions: (1) a page class reached as a value (window.File through defaultView) could not be constructed from the host — function wrappers now take a construct path (a new rpc op) instead of applying, which threw 'class constructors must be invoked with new' in the page; (2) a host subclass of a page class (every custom element class) was encoded as the base class itself — the class marker is inherited through the class chain, so the second define always saw the first class and threw 'already used'; the marker now counts only as an own property; (3) a host function the page hands back (customElements.get) arrived as a fresh wrapper, not the same function — the guest marks its host-function wrappers and echoes them back by id.

ACCEPTED COMPLETE on 2026-11-04 by the author. Measured in Phase 4, reproducible via scripts/tl-suite.mjs: @testing-library/dom's own suite (v10.4.2, 657 tests, the version this package tests against) passes 657/657 under its jsdom environment and 654/657 under this package's jest environment. The three that fail only under ours are accepted as out-of-scope/environment factors, not DOM gaps: two (fake-timers: waitFor's requestAnimationFrame under legacy and modern jest fake timers) are the bridged-realm architecture — jest's fake timers replace the test realm's globals, but the page has its own clock and its own rAF, so the fake clock cannot drive the page the way it drives jsdom's single-realm window; one (role: accessible names from ::before/::after 'which logs errors in jsdom') asserts jsdom's own console-error logging for pseudo-element computed styles, a jsdom behaviour, not a DOM contract. On the agreed acceptance line — no failures outside the out-of-scope/environment set — the suite passes.

accepted.what: RESIDUAL (2026-11-04): jest legacy fake timers replace only the test realm's clock; the page keeps its own setTimeout/rAF, so waitFor's fake-timer branch cannot drive it. Stays on jsdom. See docs/environment-triage.md.
RESIDUAL (2026-11-04): same bridged-realm reason as the legacy entry; modern fake timers advance the test realm, not the page's clock. Stays on jsdom. See docs/environment-triage.md.

RESIDUAL (2026-11-04): the test asserts jsdom's own console-error logging for ::before/::after computed styles; that is jsdom behaviour, not a DOM contract. Stays on jsdom. See docs/environment-triage.md.

policies.fakeTimers: real-timer tests migrate (tests/env/testing-library.test.ts:71-95); fake-timer tests remain on jsdom
policies.raf: page requestAnimationFrame is a 16ms page setTimeout; visual=false removes the globals; fake timers never advance the page clock — see docs/environment-triage.md section 3
policies.externalResources: the env setup does not await dom.ready and exposes no dom; external scripts/resources are unsupported by the env (use plain JSDOM and await dom.ready)
policies.teardown: dom.close() is synchronous and does not await in-flight fetch/scripts/microtasks; use the disposal procedure in docs/environment-triage.md section 5; the failing reproduction is still pending (要再現)
